## Data Exploration

Import some packages

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

- First lets import NFL data

```{r}
nfl_data <- read.csv("data/NFL_2009_2018.csv")
```

- lets check the structure of the data out

```{r}

str(nfl_data)
```

- There are many columns so lets try to work with a smaller subset of columns

```{r}

sub_nfl_data <- nfl_data |> select(home_team, 
                                   away_team,
                                   yardline_100,
                                   game_date,
                                   down,
                                   time,
                                   ydstogo,
                                   play_type,
                                   pass_length,
                                   pass_location,
                                   yards_gained,
                                   run_location,
                                   quarter_seconds_remaining,
                                   side_of_field,
                                   shotgun,
                                   qb_dropback,
                                   posteam,
                                   air_yards,
                                   run_location,
                                   qb_dropback
                                   )
sub_nfl_data
```

- Lets check out some contingency tables

```{r}
# 2 way contingency table for yards to go and play type
table(sub_nfl_data$ydstogo, sub_nfl_data$play_type)

# 2 way contingency table for down and play type
table(sub_nfl_data$down, sub_nfl_data$play_type)

# 2 way contingency table for pass_length and pass_location
table(sub_nfl_data$pass_length, sub_nfl_data$pass_location)

# 1 way contingency table for play type, run_locaiton, pass_length
table(sub_nfl_data$play_type)
table(sub_nfl_data$run_location)
table(sub_nfl_data$pass_length)
```

- Lets create some numerical summaries for quantitative variables at levels of categorical variables

```{r}

#summary stats for yards gained from each pass location
tapply(sub_nfl_data$yards_gained, 
       sub_nfl_data$pass_location, 
       function(x) c(
         mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
       ))

#summary stats for yard line a certain play type is made
tapply(sub_nfl_data$yardline_100, 
       sub_nfl_data$play_type,
       function(x) c(
         mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
       ))
#summary stats for yards gained when in shotgun
tapply(sub_nfl_data$yards_gained,
       sub_nfl_data$shotgun,
       function(x) c(
         mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
         sd = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
       ))

```

- Lets plot some of these variables using different plots/graphs

```{r}
#First we will make a boxplot for the type of play run depeding on the yards to go for first down
plot_1 <- sub_nfl_data |>
  filter(!is.na(down),
         !is.na(play_type),
         !is.na(ydstogo)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x= play_type,y= ydstogo)) +
  facet_wrap(~ down) +
  geom_boxplot(na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Play Type",
       y = "Yards to go for First Down",
       title = "Play Type Based on Yards to Go and Down") +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
plot_1 
```

```{r}
#Create a histogram 
plot_2 <- sub_nfl_data |>
  filter(!is.na(yards_gained))|>
  ggplot(aes(x = yards_gained)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, 
                 na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Yards Gained",
    y = "Frequency",
    title = "Distribution of Yards Gained on Each down"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
plot_2
```

```{r}
#stacked bar chart
plot_3 <- sub_nfl_data|>
  filter(!is.na(down),
         !is.na(play_type),
         !is.na(posteam)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = down,fill = play_type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill",
           na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~posteam)
  labs(
    x = "Down",
    y = "Play Type Proportion",
    title = "Proportion of Play Type Based on Team and Down"
  )
plot_3
```

```{r}
#box plot
plot_4 <- sub_nfl_data |>
  filter(!is.na(play_type),
         !is.na(yards_gained),
         !is.na(down),
         !is.na(shotgun)) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = play_type,
    y = yards_gained,
    fill = factor(shotgun)
  )) +
  geom_boxplot(size = 0.5) +
  labs(
    x = "Play Type",
    y = "Yards Gained",
    fill = "Shotgun (0 = No, 1 = Yes)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
  
plot_4
```

```{r}
#Scatter plot
plot_5 <- sub_nfl_data |>
  filter(!is.na(air_yards),
         !is.na(yards_gained),
         !is.na(pass_location),
         !is.na(down)) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = air_yards,
    y = yards_gained,
    color = pass_location
  )) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~down) +
  labs(
    x = "Air Yards",
    y = "Yards Gained",
    title = "Air Yards Gained Based on Down and Pass Location"
  )
plot_5
```

```{r}
plot_6 <- sub_nfl_data |>
  filter(
    !is.na(down),
    !is.na(air_yards),
    !is.na(yards_gained)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = yards_gained,
    y = air_yards,
  )) +
  geom_bin2d(bins = 30)+
  facet_wrap(~down)
  labs(
    title = "Average Yards Gained by Down and Distance",
    x = "Yards to Go",
    y = "Down",
    fill = "Avg. Yards"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

plot_6
```
